subject: Hybrid commit + on-demand surcharge structure
body:
From: Sanjay Reddy <sanjay@nimbuspay.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: Maya Lin <maya.lin@nimbuspay.com>
Date: 2026-10-11T09:12:00Z
Subject: Re: hybrid commit + on-demand structure — initial ask

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency and cost numbers looked great. We ran a quick internal model of our forecast and wanted to propose something slightly different from a straight reserve:

- We expect a baseline of ~60B tokens/month for Q1 (primarily embeddings + short chat).
- We’d like a 70/30 split: 70% covered by commit (discounted per-token), 30% on-demand.
- For on-demand above commit we are looking for a capped surcharge model rather than a single flat overage rate — something like a stepped surcharge that softens after big spikes.

Attached is our spend model (Nimbus_Spend_Model_v3.xlsx) with token distributions. Can Redwood sketch a term sheet that shows: committed monthly $ amount -> effective per-token price; on-demand surcharge tiers (0-10% above commit, 10-50%, 50%+); and an example true-up if we miss commit by >20%?

Also, our procurement will push for a minimum commitment floor that’s refundable/creditable if we hit certain growth milestones. Happy to take a call to walk through.

Thanks,
Sanjay
Head of Platform, NimbusPay

-----

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Sanjay Reddy <sanjay@nimbuspay.com>
Cc: Maya Lin <maya.lin@nimbuspay.com>, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-11T14:05:00Z
Subject: Re: hybrid commit + on-demand structure — initial ask

Sanjay — thanks, appreciated.

We can definitely model a hybrid approach. High level thoughts up front:
- Commit (reserved dollars): deep per-token discount and priority routing for latency-sensitive traffic.
- On-demand portion: priced at standard hosted rate with a surcharge ladder that steps down as utilization normalizes (we can do automatic smoothing credits after monthly true-up).
- Refundable/creditable portion: we can offer a time-bound credit bucket that converts into usage credits if you meet growth milestones across quarters.

I’ve looped in Marcus (pricing) and Lauren (legal/go-to-market constraints). We’ll produce a short term sheet showing a few numeric examples based on your attached model. Can you confirm whether the 60B tokens for Q1 is seasonally smoothed month-to-month or concentrated into a couple high-traffic months? That affects the surge bands.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive — Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

-----

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-11T16:20:00Z
Subject: INTERNAL: Draft numbers for Nimbus — hybrid proposal

Kim / Lauren — I put together a quick draft term structure (internal only) before we send to Nimbus:

1) Commit tier: $25,000/month (min 12-month) — covers ~62.5B tokens/month at an effective rate of $0.0004/token (post-discount).
   - Quarterly true-up with credits applied if growth milestones hit (see milestone table).
2) On-demand base rate: $0.0009/token.
3) Surcharge ladder (applies only to on-demand tokens when monthly usage > commit):
   - 0–10% above commit: +12% surcharge (effective on-demand $0.001008/token)
   - 10–50% above commit: +7% surcharge (effective $0.000963/token)
   - >50% above commit: +2% surcharge (effective $0.000918/token)
   Rationale: we want to avoid punitive step-functions — larger spikes should get better marginal pricing to avoid breaking the app.
4) Missed-commit protection: if Nimbus is >20% below committed monthly usage for two consecutive months, we offer a one-time catch-up credit equal to 20% of that month’s committed-dollar shortfall, provided they meet the next quarter’s growth milestone.
5) Refundable floor: up to $75k of the first-year commitment can be held as a refundable credit that unlocks over four quarters conditioned on usage/expansion.

I think this gives them predictability (deep commit discount) + flexible protection for spikes. Legal will need to scope refundable-credit language and true-up timing. Thoughts?

—Marcus
Senior Pricing Analyst

-----

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-11T18:03:00Z
Subject: Re: INTERNAL: Draft numbers for Nimbus — hybrid proposal

Marcus — looks sensible. A couple points before we externalize:
- Make sure the refundable-credit mechanism is explicitly labeled as a "usage credit" (non-refundable cash) to keep accounting clean. Procurement will push for refundability; we should hold firm unless legal signs off an exception.
- Define the monthly true-up window clearly (e.g., 30 days after month end) and how credits apply (applied to next invoice only).
- Add an early-termination claw if they want to take capacity elsewhere within first 6 months; claw limited to unused refundable credit.

If you can produce a one-page term sheet PDF, I’ll review and then Kim can send to Nimbus.

—Lauren
Head of GTM & Contracts

-----

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Sanjay Reddy <sanjay@nimbuspay.com>, Maya Lin <maya.lin@nimbuspay.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-12T11:09:00Z
Subject: Redwood term sheet: hybrid commit + surge smoothing (draft) 

Sanjay / Maya — attaching a concise term sheet that maps your 70/30 split into concrete numbers (redwood_hybrid_commit_term_sheet.pdf). Highlights:

- Commit: $25k/mo (12-mo) -> effective $0.0004/token (covers ~62.5B tokens).
- On-demand base: $0.0009/token with a three-step surcharge ladder that eases marginal pricing as spikes grow (see table).
- Missed commit: two-month consecutive shortfall >20% triggers a one-time catch-up usage credit (20% of shortfall $).
- Refundable credit: up to $75k in year-one credits; labeled as usage credits applied to invoices (not cash refunds). Unlock schedule in sheet.
- True-up timing: monthly true-up, invoice adjustment applied within 45 days.

A few open items we’d like your input on before finalizing:
1) Do you prefer surcharge ladder applied to on-demand tokens only (current) or across total usage once spikes occur?
2) Are the proposed milestones for refundable-credit unlock achievable for Nimbus (I pasted a short milestone table in the sheet)?
3) Any procurement constraints around the 12-month minimum?

Next steps: if this looks reasonable, we can hand the draft to Legal and Procurement to convert into a short amendment for signature.

Attachments: redwood_hybrid_commit_term_sheet.pdf (term table + example calculations)

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive — Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment stub: redwood_hybrid_commit_term_sheet.pdf (1.2MB, PDF)

-----

From: Sanjay Reddy <sanjay@nimbuspay.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: Maya Lin <maya.lin@nimbuspay.com>
Date: 2026-10-13T16:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Redwood term sheet: hybrid commit + surge smoothing (draft)

Kim — thanks, got the sheet and numbers look close to our target. Quick answers:

1) Surcharge ladder: prefer it to remain on on-demand tokens only — we want commit to be sacrosanct for predictability.
2) Milestones: the unlock schedule looks reasonable; I’ll confirm the Q1 month distribution (we currently plan a ramp — will upload a revised spend model).
3) Procurement: 12-month min is acceptable if the refundable-credit stays as "usage credits" (not cash). They will still ask for a short SLT approval on the refundable credit but I think we can move forward.

Please go ahead and open a legal ticket and we’ll queue our procurement for the doc review. We’d like to close by the end of October if possible.

Best,
Sanjay
Head of Platform, NimbusPay
